notes: Functional property (RBox 0018). The original holds by definition, with no exceptions: Wikipedia (Enclave and exclave, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enclave_and_exclave) defines an enclave as "a territory that is entirely surrounded by the territory of only one other state or entity", and a territory surrounded by more than one state is not an enclave (Nakhchivan is the article's example). Nested cases (Baarle, Nahwa/Madha) do not break it: a counter-enclave is the outer state's own territory, an enclave only within the middle state. Functionality follows from no other tag of enclave_within (asymmetric, inverse:completely_surrounds), so its delete is clean. The edit removes functionality; the instance questions ask whether the given fact is consistent with the enclave also being an enclave within a second state: original no, new yes (without functionality nothing rules it out). Instances are the true sovereign enclaves Lesotho and San Marino. The zh prompt uses 内飞地 (enclave, as opposed to 外飞地, exclave) with no gloss: a gloss 'completely surrounded by South Africa' would add a geometric fact that rules out Botswana without functionality. Direct and instance answers are new 'yes', balancing 0017's new 'no'. Near: functionality of capital_of (reference no, differs from the new answer). Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer. Verifier (round 2): instance questions rephrased from 'Can X at the same time be...?' to 'Is it consistent with this fact that X is also...?', so the answer rests on the given fact and the property only, not on world knowledge that Lesotho does not touch Botswana; answers unchanged (original no, new yes), so the topic's RBox yes/no balance stays 3/3.
